checks.message: Notebook instance storage not encrypted with a KMS key
checks.context: Notebook instances store model code, training data, and credentials on EBS. Without a KMS key, that storage is encrypted with an AWS-managed key with no audit trail.

checks.message: No subnet specified — notebook may be deployed with direct internet access
checks.context: Without a subnet, SageMaker gives the notebook direct outbound internet access, bypassing your VPC network controls. Notebooks should run in private subnets with internet access via NAT.

checks.message: Direct internet access enabled on notebook instance
checks.context: A notebook with direct internet access is reachable from the public internet and can exfiltrate data or download malicious packages without going through your VPC controls. Disable it and use NAT.

checks.message: Verify output S3 bucket has encryption and access controls configured
checks.context: Training job output (model artifacts) is written to the S3 location specified in --output-data-config. If that bucket is misconfigured, your trained models — which may encode sensitive training data — are exposed.

checks.message: Verify the execution role is scoped to only the S3 buckets and resources this job needs
checks.context: Training job roles with s3:* can read every bucket in your account. If your training data includes PII, a misconfigured role can expose it to other jobs or services.

checks.message: Verify the endpoint has authentication — SageMaker endpoints require IAM auth by default but can be misconfigured
checks.context: SageMaker real-time endpoints require AWS SigV4 signing by default. If you're fronting the endpoint with API Gateway or Lambda, ensure those layers enforce authentication before passing requests through.

checks.message: Endpoint deletion is immediate — any application calling it will fail instantly
checks.context: There is no graceful drain for SageMaker endpoints. All in-flight requests fail immediately. Update your application to stop sending traffic before deleting.

checks.message: Face collections store biometric data — verify your data handling complies with GDPR, CCPA, and BIPA
checks.context: Facial recognition data is biometric PII under most privacy laws. Storing faces without explicit consent and a documented retention/deletion policy is a legal liability in many jurisdictions.

checks.message: Deleting a collection permanently removes all indexed faces
checks.context: All face vectors stored in the collection are destroyed. Any application using this collection for face search or verification will fail immediately.

checks.message: Verify training data in S3 doesn't contain unredacted PII
checks.context: Comprehend training jobs read from S3. If your training documents contain names, SSNs, or medical data, that data is processed by the service and stored in the output bucket. Redact PII before training.

checks.message: Verify the bot doesn't log sensitive user inputs to CloudWatch
checks.context: Lex conversation logs capture everything users say to the bot, including passwords, credit card numbers, and PII if users type them. Enable PII redaction in conversation logs or disable logging for sensitive bots.

checks.message: Verify the output S3 bucket is private and the text input doesn't contain sensitive data
checks.context: Polly writes audio files to S3. If the input text contains PII or confidential content and the output bucket is public, that content is exposed as an audio file.

checks.message: Review data privacy settings before translating sensitive content
checks.context: AWS AI services have an opt-out policy configurable via Organizations AI services opt-out policies. If you're translating confidential documents or PII, verify your organization's opt-out settings and consider using a custom terminology endpoint.

checks.message: Verify the dataset import role is scoped to only the S3 bucket containing forecast data
checks.context: Forecast assumes the IAM role you provide to read training data from S3. A role with s3:* can read every bucket in your account. Scope it to the specific bucket and prefix.

checks.message: Endpoint config not encrypted with a customer managed KMS key
checks.context: Without a KMS key, model artifacts are encrypted with an AWS-managed key with no audit trail. For sensitive models, specify a CMK for full control over access and rotation.

checks.message: Verify the execution role is scoped to only the S3 buckets containing model artifacts
checks.context: The model execution role is used at inference time. A role with broad S3 or network access could be exploited if the model container is compromised. Scope to specific resource ARNs.

checks.message: Verify the notebook instance has internet access disabled if it doesn't need it
checks.context: Starting a notebook with direct internet access allows it to download packages and exfiltrate data. If the notebook doesn't need outbound internet, ensure it's in a private subnet.

checks.message: Stopping preserves data on the attached EBS volume but terminates the ML compute instance
checks.context: Any running processes, unsaved work in memory, and active kernel sessions are lost. Data saved to the EBS volume (/home/ec2-user/SageMaker) is preserved.

checks.message: Verify the update doesn't enable direct internet access or change the KMS key
checks.context: Updating a notebook can change its network configuration, instance type, and IAM role. Enabling direct internet access or switching to a less restricted role weakens the notebook's security posture.
